correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the unique u–v path length ell leaves an (ell+1)-rooted forest extension, counted with weighted Cayley identity. The third vertex w lies on the interior path with probability (ell−1)/(n−2); if off path its degree is 1+Bin(n−ell−2,1/n), if on path 2+Bin(n−ell−2,1/n)+Bern(1/(ell+1)). This yields the stated exact generating-function mixture; terminal ell=n−1 has deterministic D=2. Subtracting adjacent tail generating functions gives a quadratic with positive constant, negative leading coefficient for ell>=2. Convolution by A(z)^h, A(z)>0 coefficientwise, cannot introduce additional alternating sign changes, while first and last terms remain opposite, proving exactly one positive-to-negative tail crossing. Ell1→2 is all-positive, terminal comparison explicit, and the conditional means increase by a rational positive difference. Independently enumerated every Prüfer code at n=3..6, checked exact laws and all threshold signs, and verified coefficient and one-crossing identities for n4..50. The algebraic proof, not bounded enumeration, establishes universality.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks corroborate exact identities only; all-parameter assertions depend on the reconstructed proof and named published premises.

originality.rationale: The weighted Cayley forest formula and the conditional one-point marginal are classical, and a published endpoint-degree/marked-distance theorem establishes opposite-sign stochastic regression when the degree is at a distance endpoint. This paper studies a distinct third vertex, where means increase but tail laws exhibit exactly one sign change rather than domination. The full crossing theorem is not a corollary of the known endpoint law nor of Janson distance-profile limit theorems.
residual_risks: Classical total-positivity or multivariate tree-enumeration literature could imply a more general variation-diminishing tail theorem.
Not all older forest enumerations were inspected in full.

value.rationale: Conditional third-vertex degree is natural when two other vertices are fixed as a geometric reference pair. Its stochastic behavior is qualitatively subtler than endpoint regression: strictly increasing means coexist with opposing tails and a unique sign reversal at each noninitial distance step. The uniform exact classification of all thresholds is a motivated dependence theorem, not just computing one marginal.
residual_risks: No extension to conditioned Galton–Watson laws or endpoint degree.

limitations: Uniform Cayley-labelled tree only, three distinct vertices.
For n3 only two distances and no claimed later crossing; the main dichotomy states n>=4.
Finite Prüfer checks are not infinite proof.
